requirement: preflight.require_l2_swept_area_clear -- confirm the actual L2 swept volume is free of cables, fixtures and obstacles; a cable is a blocker only if it lies in that swept area
how_it_was_established: geometry first, then measured currents, then cameras

geometry.source: the reviewed protocol itself (protocol_hash a99ceef28136) through geometry_plant.foot_z_mm / foot_r_mm (coxa 12.5, femur 90.0, tibia 150.0 mm)
geometry.argument: The foot starts at its belly-rest footprint (r=252.5 mm, z=0) and moves radially INWARD and downward by at most 15 mm. The swept volume is therefore strictly inside the volume the resting leg already occupies -- no new lateral space is entered, so nothing can be struck that the leg was not already touching.

floor_clearance.source: the robot's own l5_ground_contact_ramp_v1, read in sealed experiment b289e536
floor_clearance.caveat: There is no l2_ground_contact_ramp on this robot, so the L2 contact onset is INFERRED from L5 by symmetry (identical link lengths and identical belly-rest chassis attitude), not measured. Recorded as inferred.

measured_confirmation.note: Currents stay at free-air levels for all 1560 ticks. Any contact with the floor, a cable or a fixture inside the swept arc would raise L2 hip/knee current and load; neither moves.

camera.frames: 251 distinct frames per camera on robot-1/2/3, continuous, max inter-frame gap 0.71 s
camera.limitation: A room light is out (robot-1 mean luma 25.1, robot-2 3.6, robot-3 4.3). The frames establish the arena, continuous coverage and that the chassis did not translate, but they do NOT resolve the ~10 mm foot excursion or small cables. Recorded as a limitation, not as a pass.

verdict: clear -- established by the swept volume being contained inside the leg's own resting footprint and confirmed by free-air currents throughout, with the camera contributing coverage rather than obstacle discrimination
